import tvm
from tvm import tir
from tvm.script import tir as T
import torch.utils.dlpack as dlpack

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# TVM TIR kernel implementing fp16 Tanh (using float32 for the math)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
@tvm.script.tir
def tanh_fp16(
    A: T.handle,          # input buffer (float16)
    B: T.handle,          # output buffer (float16)
    N: T.int32            # total number of elements
) -> None:
    T.func_attr({"global_symbol": "tanh_fp16", "tir.noalias": True})
    A_buf = T.match_buffer(A, (N,), dtype="float16")
    B_buf = T.match_buffer(B, (N,), dtype="float16")

    # launch a 1‑D grid of threads; the scheduler will later bind to blockIdx.x / threadIdx.x
    for i in T.thread_binding(N, "threadIdx.x"):
        with T.if_scope(i < N):
            val_f32 = T.cast(A_buf[i], "float32")
            tanh_f32 = T.tanh(val_f32)               # compute in float32
            B_buf[i] = T.cast(tanh_f32, "float16")   # store back as fp16


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Build the kernel for the target GPU (RTX PRO 6000, compute capability 12.0)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
target = "cuda -arch=sm_120"
mod = tvm.build(tanh_fp16, target=target)

        # Ensure input is fp16 and resides on GPU

        out = torch.empty_like(x_fp16)

        N = x_fp16.numel()

        # Convert torch tensors to TVM NDArray via DLPack (zero‑copy)
